relearning.title: Read: the plant kingdom
relearning.description: A short reading with the plumbing analogy, worked examples and quick checks.

sections.title: What makes a plant, and the four groups

body.text:
**I can give a general description of the organisms in the Kingdom Plantae.**

**What all plants share:** they are **multicellular eukaryotes**, they are **autotrophs** that make their own food by **photosynthesis** using chlorophyll in chloroplasts, and their cell walls are made of **cellulose**. Most live on land.

**Think of the plumbing in a building.** Pipes carry water up to every floor. Without pipes, you could only build a one-story shack where water soaks in from the ground. Plants with "pipes" are **vascular plants**. Their pipes are **vascular tissue**: **xylem** carries water up from the roots, and **phloem** carries sugar from the leaves to the rest of the plant.

**The four main groups:**
- **Nonvascular plants (mosses):** no vascular tissue, so they stay small and live in damp places. They reproduce with spores.
- **Seedless vascular plants (ferns):** have vascular tissue but no seeds. They reproduce with spores (the brown dots under a fern leaf).
- **Gymnosperms (conifers, like pines):** vascular plants with seeds that form in **cones**. "Gymnosperm" means "naked seed": the seed is not inside a fruit.
- **Angiosperms (flowering plants):** vascular plants with **flowers**, and seeds inside a **fruit**. This is the largest group.

**Worked example:** Wisconsin's state tree, the sugar maple. It has vascular tissue (it grows tall), it makes seeds, and it has flowers and fruit (the winged "helicopters" carry its seeds). It is an **angiosperm**.

checks.prompt: Why do mosses stay small and grow in damp places?

options.text: They have no vascular tissue to carry water up

checks.explanation: Mosses are nonvascular, so water just soaks from cell to cell and can't reach very high. They do photosynthesize, and they make spores, not seeds.

checks.prompt: A white pine makes its seeds in cones and has no flowers. Which group is it in?
checks.explanation: Seeds in cones with no flowers or fruit means gymnosperm. Angiosperms have flowers and seeds inside a fruit.

sections.title: Living on land, and spores versus seeds

body.text:
**Plant parts.** **Roots** hold the plant in place and absorb water and minerals. **Stems** hold the plant up and contain the xylem and phloem. **Leaves** are where most photosynthesis happens.

**Adaptations for life on land:**
- A **waxy cuticle** on leaves keeps water from evaporating.
- **Stomata** are tiny openings in leaves that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapor out.
- **Vascular tissue** moves water and food, so plants can grow tall.
- **Seeds** carry a baby plant and its food inside a protective coat, so it can wait for good conditions.
- **Pollen** carries sperm through the air or on animals, so seed plants don't need water to reproduce.

**Spores vs. seeds.** A spore is a single cell with no stored food. A seed holds a tiny plant (embryo) plus food, inside a coat. Mosses and ferns use spores. Gymnosperms and angiosperms use seeds.

**Worked example 2:** A fern grows in a shady Wisconsin woods. It is about knee-high (it has vascular tissue), it has no flowers or cones, and the dots under its leaves release spores. It is a **seedless vascular plant**.

**Worked example 3:** Corn and beans are both angiosperms. Corn is a **monocot**: one seed leaf and parallel veins. Beans are **dicots**: two seed leaves and veins that branch like a net.

**Watch out for:** thinking every plant makes seeds (mosses and ferns don't), mixing up xylem (water, up from the roots) and phloem (sugar, from the leaves), calling a pine cone a fruit, and calling algae plants.

checks.prompt: A plant has vascular tissue, makes no seeds and reproduces with spores. Which group is it in?
checks.explanation: Vascular tissue but no seeds means a seedless vascular plant, like a fern. Mosses use spores too, but they have no vascular tissue.

checks.prompt: Type the vascular tissue that carries water up from the roots.
checks.explanation: Xylem carries water up from the roots. Phloem carries sugar from the leaves, which is the common mix-up.

sections.shortAnswer: Explain why having vascular tissue lets a plant grow taller than a moss.

relearning.title: Do: flip the plant cards, then sort plants with three questions
relearning.description: Flashcards with a 3-question self-quiz, then a plant classified one question at a time.

cards.back: Multicellular eukaryotes that make their own food by photosynthesis. Cell walls of cellulose.
Vascular tissue that carries water up from the roots.
Vascular tissue that carries sugar from the leaves to the rest of the plant.
Plants with no vascular tissue, like mosses. Small, live in damp places, use spores.
Plants with vascular tissue but no seeds, like ferns. They use spores.
Seed plants whose seeds form in cones, not fruit, like pines and spruces.
Flowering plants whose seeds grow inside a fruit, like maples, apples and grasses.

checks.prompt: Which tissue carries sugar from the leaves to the rest of the plant?
checks.explanation: Phloem carries sugar (food). Xylem carries water up from the roots, which is the common mix-up.

checks.prompt: Which plant reproduces with spores instead of seeds?
checks.explanation: Ferns (and mosses) use spores. Pines and apple trees are seed plants.

checks.prompt: What is true of every plant?

options.text: It makes its own food by photosynthesis

checks.explanation: All plants are autotrophs that photosynthesize. Only angiosperms make flowers, and mosses have no vascular tissue.

sections.title: Worked problem: classify a plant with three questions

body.problem: Classify a white pine using three yes-or-no questions. Q1: Does it have vascular tissue? (No → nonvascular plant.) Q2: Does it make seeds? (No → seedless vascular plant.) Q3: Does it have flowers and fruit? (No → gymnosperm. Yes → angiosperm.)

steps.text: Q1: Does a white pine have vascular tissue? Yes. It grows more than 30 meters tall, which takes xylem to carry water up. Go on to Q2.
Q2: Does it make seeds? Yes. Its seeds form inside its cones. Go on to Q3.
Q3: Does it have flowers and fruit? No. The seeds sit on the scales of the cone, not inside a fruit.
Answer: the white pine is a gymnosperm ("naked seed").

checks.prompt: Your turn: which plant would stop at Q1 because it has no vascular tissue?
checks.explanation: Mosses are nonvascular, so they answer "no" at Q1. Ferns and maples both have vascular tissue.

checks.prompt: An apple tree has vascular tissue, makes seeds, and grows flowers that become apples. Which group is it in?
checks.explanation: Yes, yes and yes: flowers and seeds inside a fruit (the apple) make it an angiosperm. Calling it a gymnosperm misses the flowers and fruit.
